open_issues: Shared-scope limitation that the narrowed RollbackAsync cannot remove: CorrespondenceService's SaveChangesAsync inside the registration transaction also flushes whatever else the shared session-scoped WakeelDb happens to be tracking, so the transaction rollback discards those rows from the database while their entities are left looking saved (Unchanged). The new test asserts only what the narrowing does control — another screen's in-memory values and its newly added entity are no longer reloaded away or detached. A complete fix would give the numbering transaction its own DbContext, which is an architecture decision outside this package.

ReminderScheduler's public constructor gained a fifth parameter (Correspondence.IFollowUpService). The only direct construction in the tree was tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests/DailyShellWorld.cs, which was updated; every other consumer resolves it from the Core DI extension, where IFollowUpService is already registered. If a package outside src/Wakeel.Core or tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests constructs it by hand, that call site needs the extra argument.

CoreAr.cs, HealthService.cs and HealthServiceTests.cs are also carried as modified by other concurrent packages in the same working tree; my edits to them are confined to the Isolate helper, the formatters named in ruling 4, and the two composed-string assertions those formatters broke.
notes:
Per finding, with the supervisor rulings applied.

FINDING 1 (medium — draft promoted to «جديد» with no number). CorrespondenceService.ChangeStatusAsync now refuses a Draft source immediately after LoadAsync and before EnsureTransition, throwing CorrespondenceRefusedException(CoreAr.CorrRefusedDraftNeedsNumbering). The identical guard was added in FollowUpService.AddAsync inside the `if (statusTo is { } target)` block, beside the Cancelled/Closed/Archived refusal. The Arabic string («المسودة تصبح جديدة بتسجيل الوارد أو اعتماد الصادر، وعندها يصدر رقمها») had already been placed in CoreAr by the attempt that was cut off; it is now used. Two tests in CorrespondenceStateMachineTests assert both doors refuse, the wording carries no Latin letter or digit, the row is still «مسودة» with OfficialNumber null and the incoming sequence still at 0, no follow-up row was written, and the draft is still accepted by DeleteDraftAsync.

FINDING 2 / RULING 1 (medium — follow-up reminders never ran). ReminderScheduler's primary constructor gained Correspondence.IFollowUpService, and RunOnceAsync calls followUps.RunDueRemindersAsync(utcNow, cancellationToken) after the backup pass, folding Created/Skipped into the aggregate before the badge invalidation and the sweep — so it is counted, and the badge is invalidated when a follow-up reminder rings. CorrespondenceWorld and DailyShellWorld now build the scheduler with the real FollowUpService. New test A_due_follow_up_rings_through_the_whole_reminder_pass_exactly_once drives the whole scheduler: nothing of that kind before the instant, exactly one notification at the due instant, and a second identical pass creates nothing more.

RULINGS 2 and 3 — closed with no code change (soft delete of an unnumbered draft stays; migration 0003 and the SchemaTests index name stay).

FINDING 7 / RULING 4 (bidi isolates in stored text). CoreAr gained a public Isolate(string?) helper wrapping a value in U+2068 … U+2069, documented as needed because the sentences are composed once and stored. Applied to every CorrAudit* formatter that embeds a caller value (DraftCreated, Registered, Approved, Cancelled — both halves —, Closed, DraftDeleted, Corrected, Referred, the new ReferralStatus, Exported, Imported) and to the Health* sentences that embed a size, version, model name, free/total space, relative backup date, sync instant, version+build date and report timestamp. HealthSyncDevice isolates only the time half, since the device label is a fixed Arabic word. Test Stored_audit_lines_isolate_the_number_and_the_file_name_they_embed reads the rows back out of audit_log, asserts the isolate pair surrounds the official number in both the registration and the cancellation line, asserts that stripping the pair gives back the plain sentence, and spot-checks the exported/imported/approved and two health formatters.

FINDING 3 (recipient-only export honoured a caller key). ExportAsync now ignores request.RecipientPublicKey when row.RecipientOnly is true and takes the key only from ResolveRecipientKeyAsync (structure or party profile), refusing with CoreAr.CorrExchangeNoRecipientKey when there is none. Test: a recipient-only approved letter addressed to a unit with no X25519 key is refused even though a valid RecipientPublicKey is supplied, and no file is written to the output folder.

FINDING 4 (RecipientOnly did not travel). ExchangeMessage gained `public bool RecipientOnly { get; init; }` (FormatVersion stays 1), set from row.RecipientOnly in ExportAsync and passed into the CorrespondenceDraftInput in ImportAsync. Test: a recipient-only letter round-trips between two activated temporary installations and the imported incoming carries RecipientOnly with RecipientOnlyAr reading «للمستلم فقط», confirmed both on the view and on the stored row.

FINDING 5 (referral transitions unaudited; referral on a withdrawn letter). ReferralService.SetStatusAsync now writes an audit row after SaveChangesAsync using the new CoreAr.CorrAuditReferralStatus(toAr, statusAr), which reuses CorrespondenceAr.Referral(status). CreateAsync refuses when the correspondence is Cancelled or Archived with CoreAr.CorrRefusedReferralStatus («المراسلة الملغاة أو المؤرشفة لا تُحال إلى أحد»). Tests: three audit rows after create + answer + close with the two status lines asserted by formatter, and a theory covering both the cancelled and the archived letter asserting the refusal wording is Latin-free and no referral was stored.

FINDING 6 (rollback swept the whole tracker). RollbackAsync takes the correspondence row and only detaches/reloads entries that are that row itself or an OfficialNumber, DuplicateReview, AuditLogEntry or ChangeLogEntry; both call sites pass the row. The sequence-gap behaviour that the original comment exists for is unchanged (the existing A_failure_after_the_number_was_issued_rolls_the_number_back_with_everything_else test still passes and the next registration still gets 001). New test A_failed_registration_leaves_another_screens_unsaved_work_alone renames one tracked party in memory and adds another, then triggers the failing registration and asserts the rename survives and the added entity is still tracked. See open_issues for the residual shared-context limitation this cannot fix.

Collateral: HealthServiceTests' two assertions that spelled out a composed string by hand now compare against CoreAr.HealthSpaceLow(...) and CoreAr.HealthSyncDevice(...), so they no longer break when a formatter's isolates change.
